issues.issue: XLCA waives any right to require demand or proceeding against any person before the Securities Administrator demands payment, yet the claim mechanics (c031) and the 'subject to satisfaction of the conditions for making a claim' qualifier in c050 make delivery of a completed Payment Notice a condition precedent. The scope of the waived demand requirement against those conditions is left open.

The clause purports to make 'no defenses, setoffs and counterclaims of any kind' valid, expressly including 'defense of fraud in the inducement or fact, or any other circumstances which would have the effect of discharging a surety'. Whether that catch-all reaches the insurer's own avoidance or rescission rights, and how far the enumerated examples limit it, is squarely construable.

An absolute bar on defenses of any kind sits against c050, which makes XLCA's obligations unconditional only 'subject to satisfaction of the conditions for making a claim'. A failure of a claim condition is either a permitted answer or a barred 'defense', and the instrument does not say which.

The full subrogation granted here is immediately cut down by the subordination clause (c044), which makes any such rights junior to indefeasible payment in full of the Owners. Reconciling the two requires deciding whether subrogation vests but is deferred or does not arise at all.

Subordination of all subrogation rights to prior payment in full of the Owners is immediately qualified by c045, which preserves XLCA's right to full payment of Reimbursement Amounts under the Indenture and Insurance Agreement. Whether reimbursement is caught by the subordination is a genuine internal tension.

The carve-out for Reimbursement Amounts cannot easily be squared with the subordination clause (c044) it immediately follows, which subordinates XLCA's recovery rights to payment in full of the Owners. The reach of 'notwithstanding the foregoing' is the question.

The clause states the Policy is neither transferable nor assignable 'in whole or in part' and then gestures at a successor securities administrator, without a clear connective making that an exception. Whether a successor administrator takes the Policy is left uncertain by the words.

Making every Payment Notice 'effective only upon actual receipt by XLCA' contradicts the deemed-receipt rules in c034 and c039, which treat notices and documents arriving after 10:00 a.m. as received at 9:00 a.m. the next Business Day. Both cannot govern the same notice.

The obligations are declared 'irrevocable, primary, absolute and unconditional' and in the same breath 'subject to satisfaction of the conditions for making a claim'. The qualifier and the absolute language pull in opposite directions on whether any condition can defeat payment.

Fee recovery depends on a 'successful action or proceeding', a term that does not say whether partial success qualifies, and on costs 'reasonably incurred'. The threshold of success is the contestable word.

Termination on 'expiration of the Term of this Policy' inherits the two competing end-dates in the Term of the Policy definition (c030) — the three cumulative conditions and the closing proviso keyed to the insurer's payments. The termination date is only as certain as that definition.

This precedence rule exists to resolve inconsistencies, and there are candidates for it to operate on — the payment-timing difference between the body (c002) and the Endorsement (c035) and the Avoided Payment conditions in c005 versus c015/c037. Applying it requires first deciding what counts as 'inconsistent'.

Entitlement to demand is keyed to 'Section 3.20 of the Indenture', an external provision not reproduced in the Policy, while the Policy's own claim mechanics (c031) state the conditions. Whether the Indenture section adds a further condition to a Policy claim is not answered internally.

The form refers to 'the Insured Note Charge off Amount (as defined below)' but nothing in the form defines it below; the cross-reference has no referent. That mechanical slip leaves the quantum of the demand resting on an absent definition.

The representation is qualified by 'based upon information available to it', which does not say what inquiry, if any, the Securities Administrator must make before certifying the Avoided Payment Amount. The qualifier's effect on the warranty is open.

'Reasonable efforts' governs the application of policy proceeds and the record-keeping, with no benchmark stated for what effort suffices. The undertaking to ensure funds are 'not applied for any other purpose' is only as strong as that undefined standard.

The Securities Administrator here assigns the Owners' claims to XLCA, while the Policy separately requires an assignment executed by each Owner in the Exhibit B form (c037, c070). Whether the form assignment or the Owner's own execution is the operative transfer is unresolved.

XLCA may 'direct all matters relating to such Insolvency Proceeding, including, without limitation' three enumerated items, so the reach of the general grant beyond preference claims, appeals and bonds is uncertain. The general-versus-specific tension is on the face of the clause.

The Owner assigns all rights or claims 'against any person relating to, arising out of or in connection with such Avoided Payment', a phrase whose outer edge — whether it sweeps in claims against originators or sponsors — cannot be fixed from the words. 'Relating to or in connection with' is the term in issue.

The Owner warrants only that the assigned claims are free of liens 'created or incurred by such Owner', while the Policy body (c002) requires the assignment accompanying a Payment Notice to be 'free of any adverse claim'. The form warrants less than the Policy demands.

The clause operates only where the form is 'reasonably determined to be insufficient' without saying by whom, and then commits the parties to 'agree on such other form as is reasonably necessary' — an agreement to agree with no default. Both the trigger and the obligation are indeterminate.
